title: Ship it! Building Production Ready Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS
talk_summary: AWS demo of building a simple dice-rolling agent in Bedrock Agents, hosting its tool in Lambda, and publishing via aliases. It is mostly a product walkthrough; the transferable parts are generic agent anatomy and LLM-readable tool schemas.

takeaways.what_they_do: They define action groups and tool parameters with natural-language descriptions and required flags so the model can decide when and how to call the tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these descriptions are read by the large language model so that it can figure out what this tool is for

takeaways.technique: Preserve tool-call history inside the agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat conversational history as operational state: reasoning steps and tool results must remain in context so the next loop iteration knows what has already happened.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it needs to remember those things that it that it's done so that um it's each next step it can do that within the context

takeaways.technique: Versioned agent aliases for staged publishing
takeaways.what_they_do: They use agent aliases to separate prepared/published versions through the software lifecycle before routing production traffic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can have different aliases as you're um uh publishing out your agents
